official.title: Doctoral Researcher (Railway wheel friction estimation and control)
official.description_text:
Tampere University and Tampere University of Applied Sciences create a unique environment for multidisciplinary, inspirational and high-impact research and education. Our universities community has its competitive edges in technology, health and society.
www.tuni.fi/en
Within the
unit of Automation Technology and Mechanical Engineering
,
faculty of Engineering and Natural Sciences
, we are recruiting one (1) doctoral positions. The unit has about 20 professors and 100 research staff in the areas of Robotics, Automation, and Mechanical engineering. Mechanical engineering is one of the core areas of education and research of the faculty. The position is opened in the Machine Design group (
Machine Dynamics Group (Machine Design) | Tampere University
).
Our group integrates machine dynamics, AI, computer vision, structural mechanics, and control for condition monitoring and asset management of railway rolling stock and infrastructure.
Job description
We are looking for one (1) Doctoral Researcher in the areas of vehicle dynamics, automatic control and mechatronics. Successful candidates will pursue a doctoral degree at Tampere University. Full-time doctoral studies are expected to be completed in three years.
You will focus on the research of experimental methods on onboard railway wheel friction estimate and control. You will collaborate closely with one doctoral researcher at Machine Dynamic Group who develops computational methods for model-based rail friction estimation. During your PhD you will have opportunity to test your technology on full-scale wheel-rail lab (
Full-Scale Wheel-Rail Lab | Tampere University
) at Tampere University and real train operated in Finland. You will have the opportunity for the research exchange in other EU countries. You will work for the project funded by Research Council of Finland (
RAILCLIMA | Tampere Universities
).
Your work will include:
Develop and validate experimental methods and advanced sensor instrumentation for onboard wheel–rail friction estimation.
Investigate the operational and environmental conditions under which wheel–rail friction can be estimated accurately and reliably.
Develop methods for wheel slip detection using existing vehicle sensor signals and operational data.
Design and implement hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation platforms for wheel friction control.
As a Doctoral Researcher you are expected to perform overviews of state of the art, to study the principles of vehicle dynamics, friction formulation, mechatronics, signal processing and vibration analysis and experimentation instrumentation. You are also expected to develop the computational algorithms, to generate experimental results, to analyze and validate them on use case(s) through comparison with the state of the art.
The results of your research will be disseminated in scientific peer-reviewed journals, international conferences, doctoral network events and events with industry. The tasks of doctoral researchers also include teaching duties that amount to approximately 5% of their annual working hours, unless there are justified reasons to the contrary.
Requirements
You need to have a master’s degree in
Mechanical engineering, with a focus on vehicle dynamics and mechatronics
Automatic control or control Engineering
Beneficial skills (not mandatory)
Experience with MATLAB, Simulink, Python, or equivalent tools for modelling, simulation, data analysis, and algorithm development.
Strong knowledge of system identification, sensor fusion, signal processing, and control systems, with the ability to apply these methods to real-world engineering challenges.
Familiarity with vehicle dynamics, wheel–rail contact mechanics, traction control, braking systems, or related transportation applications.
Successful candidates must be pursued or will be accepted to study towards a doctoral degree in the doctoral programme of the discipline. Please visit the admissions webpage
https://www.tuni.fi/en/study-with-us/programmes/doctoral-programmes
for more information on eligibility requirements.
Candidates are selected based on the level of promise that they show, and this will be evaluated on the basis of their study and research plans, their previous success in studies, and merits in writing the doctoral thesis and / or scientific publishing.
Tampere University is a unique, multidisciplinary and boldly forward-looking, evolving community. Our values are openness, diversity, responsibility, courage, critical thinking, erudition bildung, and learner-centredness. We hope that you can embrace these values and promote them in your work.
We
offer
The position will be filled for a fixed-term period of maximum three (3) years.
The starting date is beginning of 2027 or as mutually agreed. A trial period of six (6) months applies to all our new employees.
The salary will be based on both the job requirements and the employee’s personal performance in accordance with the salary system of Finnish universities. A typical starting salary for Doctoral Researchers is approximately 3000 EUR/month. The salary increases based on experience and the progress of doctoral studies.
We are inviting you to be a part of a vibrant, active and truly international research community. We value interdisciplinarity, as it allows you to expand your research network and exposes you to new perspectives and ideas to solve complex research problems and pursue novel research findings. We are strongly committed to the highest level of scientific research and the provision of high-quality doctoral education.
As a member of staff at Tampere University, you will enjoy a range of competitive benefits, such as occupational health care services, flexible work schedule, versatile research infrastructure, modern teaching facilities and a safe and inviting campus area as well as a personal fund to spend on sports and cultural activities in your free time. Please read more about
working at Tampere University
. You can also find more information about us and working and living Tampere by watching our video:
Tampere Higher Education Community - our academic playground
.
Finland is among the most stable, free and safe countries in the world, based on prominent ratings by various agencies. Tampere is the largest inland city of Finland, and the city is counted among the major academic hubs in the Nordic countries. Tampere region is the most rapidly growing urban area in Finland and home to a vibrant knowledge-intensive entrepreneurial community. The city is an industrial powerhouse that enjoys a rich cultural scene and a reputation as a centre of Finland’s information society. Tampere is also surrounded by vivid nature with forests and lakes, providing countless opportunities for easy-to-access outdoor adventures and refreshment throughout the year.

ai.summary: Tampere doctoral position in vehicle dynamics and automatic control, focusing on experimental methods for onboard railway wheel-rail friction estimation and control. Work includes sensor instrumentation, friction estimation algorithms, wheel slip detection, and hardware-in-the-loop simulation validation.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position is in vehicle dynamics, automatic control, and mechatronics—domains with no connection to human-centered systems, immersive technologies, spatial cognition, learning, collaboration, or wayfinding. The focus is on friction estimation and rail infrastructure monitoring, entirely removed from the researcher's research interests.

methodological_fit.rationale: Minimal overlap. Position requires expertise in MATLAB/Simulink, system identification, sensor fusion, signal processing, and control systems applied to vehicle/railway engineering. While the researcher has some programming capability (Unity, C#, beginner Python), the role demands specialized knowledge in control theory, real-time embedded systems, and signal processing that are not evident in the researcher's profile. Experimental work exists in both, but the domains and methods are fundamentally different.

growth_value.rationale: Limited growth value aligned with target identity. The researcher might develop MATLAB/Simulink and signal processing skills, but these are not priorities in the target capability roadmap (spatial cognition, collaborative immersive systems, wayfinding research). The embedded systems and control focus moves away from human-centered research.

strategic_value.rationale: Tampere University is a reputable institution with strong engineering research, but this position is in the Machine Design group focused on vehicle dynamics and asset management—not human-centered research. The position is funded by the Research Council of Finland (stable funding), but the research direction does not support the researcher's target identity or career trajectory in human-centred XR/HCI.

eligibility_flags: Posting requires Master's degree in mechanical engineering (vehicle dynamics/mechatronics focus), automatic control, or control engineering—researcher's MSc is in creative multimedia with XR focus; substantial domain mismatch
Posting lists 'beneficial skills' including MATLAB, Simulink, system identification, sensor fusion, signal processing, vehicle dynamics, wheel-rail contact mechanics—researcher has none of these
MSc must be completed by start date (beginning 2027); researcher is in thesis stage
risks: Core discipline mismatch: vehicle dynamics, control systems, and rail infrastructure monitoring are excluded from the researcher's target identity
Severe background gap: researcher lacks foundational knowledge in control theory, system identification, and vehicle dynamics required for this role
Skills mismatch: MATLAB/Simulink expertise required; researcher's programming is in Unity/C# and beginner Python
Career trajectory risk: this PhD would not prepare the researcher for target positions in human-centred immersive systems research
Research culture gap: this is an engineering/control systems group; the researcher's background is creative multimedia and HCI
